mathematical_scope: Exact modular Haar synthesis/analysis on power-of-two sizes, subclassing the phase12 Green mixer, plus a strong-coupling experimental variant. inv_sqrt_size uses powers of 2 and the chosen sqrt2; recursive Haar synthesis/analysis are transposes/inverses in the finite-field normalization. The explicit omega8 compatibility assertion is important for a chosen cyclotomic embedding. Strong variant resets path couplings and Haar epsilon to 1/2 and explicitly disclaims inherited small-angle bounds.
input_and_guard_coverage: Tonelli–Shanks assumes an odd prime but accepts arbitrary p without primality validation; nonresidue is explicitly rejected. Module import computes sqrt2 and checks the square/embedding using asserts. Haar functions reject non-power-of-two lengths. Class rejects n<4/non-power-of-two but does not explicitly restrict n<=2^23 or validate order/vector shape itself; inherited constructor/apply contracts govern those. apply_R slices input by self.half without an explicit length check. Inputs are reduced through modular operations.
cost_and_scaling: Haar recursions have O(n) nodes and O(log n) stack depth, but repeatedly compute modular inverses via inv_sqrt_size; unit-cost field operation and actual Python bit costs differ. Dense stage methods are inherited. Strong constructor builds additional path solvers; no timing benchmarks.
test_evidence: Phase13 checks sqrt2²=2, modular Haar inverse on selected vectors at m2..32, mixer two-sided round trips at n8..64 and strong round trips. These five modular/permutation-related methods occur after unittest.main in test_phase13 and are missed by direct invocation. No invalid-modulus/order/vector tests. Not executed.
dependency_identity: Unreviewed-body dependencies haar_adapter c73970cef77c3bdd324ec8ca3e1bc10e9b9322a44ba8b25e3a84897b8471f2d8 and unitary_mixer aff6a16c… are hash-verified and located in package/sibling paths. Exact behavior remains conditional on those bodies, their imports and stage methods.

findings.finding: The generic-looking Tonelli helper is not guarded for arbitrary modulus; its reliable intended domain is the fixed known prime. Import-time asserts bind one root choice only while assertions are enabled.
apply_R relies on a correctly sized vector. Slicing can pass unexpected lengths into Haar transforms; a parent method’s checks cannot be assumed without inspecting that exact dependency.
Strong coupling is deliberately outside the phase12 norm/cut perturbation theorem. It must remain a separate experiment even if modular inverses or two-stage vetoes succeed.

acceptance_boundary: Accept modular Haar formulas and explicit embedding/strong-parameter separation within the intended prime and dimensions. No complex unitarity, inherited cut guarantee, or runtime verification is inferred.
